items.s: Many small shops cannot ____ to pay for extra staff.
Some workers feel ____ to finish five days of work in four.
The manager wanted clear ____ before she changed the timetable.
Many people get great job ____ from helping customers.
Free lunch is one of the ____ of working for that company.

match.d: do something too quickly to do it well
able to change to suit new conditions
causing worry or tension that is hard to deal with

items.s: Workers in six countries ____ a shorter week for six months.
Employees ____ less burnout after the change.
The company ____ unnecessary meetings to save time.
Last year my manager ____ me a free day for my birthday.
Many workers ____ much better after the trial.

tfn.s: The researchers compared the trial workplaces with a group that kept the same week.
tfn.why: The text says burnout was lower "compared with a group of workplaces that did not introduce the same change".

tfn.s: Employees did the same number of hours in four days.
tfn.why: The text says it meant "fewer working hours, not the same hours squeezed into four days".

tfn.s: Most employees in the trial spent their free day with family.
tfn.why: The text says people might do many things but does not say what the trial workers did.

tfn.s: In a four-day week, everybody has to take the same day off.
tfn.why: The text says it "does not have to mean the same day off for everybody".

tfn.s: Some businesses might need staff to work different days so they can stay open.
tfn.why: The text says shops, clinics and restaurants might need staff on more flexible schedules.

pre.d: a test of a new idea to see if it works
feeling very tired and unwell because of too much work
without wasting time or effort
taking part in something
plans that say when things happen
really, in a true way
people or companies that give others jobs
pushed into a space that is too small

focus.note: Some linking words need a short idea after them, and some join two ideas. Look at the commas and the meaning.

items.s: Sara was happy ____ she finished work early.
____ the plan is popular, some bosses still dislike it.
____ you work four days, you may feel less tired.
Many workers love the idea. ____, shops still need staff every day.
____ the meeting started, everyone had a coffee.
After the complaints, the board agreed to ____ its decision.
Despite the cuts, the firm ____ its high standards.
____ lunch breaks stop the canteen from getting too crowded.
A single score cannot ____ how employees really feel about their jobs.
Higher ____ for tickets meant the railway ran extra trains.
Setting a ____ deadline helps staff avoid unnecessary stress.

match.d: employ somebody to do a job
organise or deal with a problem
limited to a small range of things
do work you did not finish earlier

items.s: By the time the trial ended, most firms ____ their meetings.
The results ____ in a scientific journal last year.
If the trial had been longer, shops ____ extra staff.
Several firms ____ their schedules since the study ended.
The small firm refused ____ extra staff.

tfn.s: The researchers compared the results with organisations that kept their usual schedules.
tfn.why: The text mentions "twelve comparison organisations that maintained their usual schedules".

tfn.s: All 141 organisations in the study were in the same country.
tfn.why: The text names six countries, from Australia to the United States.

tfn.s: The participating organisations made higher profits during the trial.
tfn.why: The text discusses wellbeing but says nothing about profits.

tfn.s: The writer warns that the findings may not apply to every workplace.
tfn.why: The text says the organisations "had chosen to take part, so the results may not apply to every workplace".

tfn.s: Fitting forty hours into four long days counts as genuinely reducing working time.
tfn.why: The text says there is "an important difference" between the two.

pre.d: the money you receive for your job each month
feeling very tired and unwell because of too much work
working together with other people
the state of being healthy and happy
the amount of work you have to do
businesses that sell things to the public
how much work is done in a certain time
people who look after someone who is old or ill

focus.note: Decide if the linking word shows contrast, result or condition. Then check what grammar follows it.

items.s: The trial was short. ____, the results were encouraging.
The firm was small. ____, it could not afford to hire extra staff.
Some employees enjoyed the change, ____ others found their workload heavier.
Staff will struggle ____ they receive enough support.
____ the extra day off, many parents still struggled with childcare.
Her excitement about the promotion was ____ by the realisation that she would have to relocate.
Many gig workers lead a ____ existence, never sure of next month's income.
The brochure relied on glowing ____ from satisfied customers rather than hard data.
Despite the merger, the company ____ most of its key staff.
Volunteers will ____ a rigorous training programme before deployment.
Critics doubt whether the benefits will ____ once the novelty has worn off.

match.d: decide that something is not worth trying or considering
introduce a plan or product more widely
able to be used in another situation

items.s: The ____ of the findings to emergency services is doubtful.
The authors acknowledge several ____ in their design.
Staff on short contracts often feel a deep sense of ____ about their income.
Early adopters spoke ____ about the change.
The ____ of the improvements is still unknown once the trial has ended.

tfn.s: The sample may not represent employers in general.
tfn.why: Participating organisations "were willing to experiment", so their experiences may not translate to every sector.

tfn.s: The biggest wellbeing gains were found among people who cut their hours the most.
tfn.why: The text says individuals who reduced hours more "tended to experience greater wellbeing gains".

tfn.s: The writer treats the trial as proof that shorter weeks suit every sector.
tfn.why: The text calls it "neither a universal prescription" nor an excuse to dismiss shorter hours.

tfn.s: The control companies later moved to shorter weeks themselves.
tfn.why: The text only says the twelve control companies were used for comparison.

tfn.s: The trial asked staff to fit a full week's workload into fewer days.
tfn.why: The text says "This was not simply an instruction to deliver a conventional week's workload in four compressed days".

working together with others to achieve something
the way something works or produces a result
the order in which tasks are done in a job

the main, eye-catching claim about something

focus.note: Some linkers join clauses, some sit at the start of a sentence, and some are formal. Check the punctuation and the logic.

items.s: ____ the encouraging headlines, the sample was self-selected.
Staff reported feeling better, ____ not necessarily producing more.
Office staff often gain flexibility. ____, shift workers frequently gain none.
Pay was protected; ____, many workers backed the scheme.
The model could succeed, ____ the savings are reinvested in staffing.

speak.title: Role-play: a four-day week for our team
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your shop is open seven days a week. An employee wants to try a four-day week with the same pay. Ask at least two questions before you decide. You can say yes, no, or yes with a condition.

b.text: You'd like a four-day week with the same pay. Explain why it would help you and how the work will still get done. Suggest a trial.

phrases: I'd like to ask about a four-day week.
I'd still finish all my tasks.
Who'd look after the customers on that day?
We're open seven days a week, so that's a problem.
Could we try it for three months?
I'm happy to say yes if the results are good.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the manager agree, and was the plan fair for the rest of the team?
